question: Should OpenClaw standardize `openclaw commands` as the operator-facing catalog, and which JSON fields, plugin metadata, and Gateway relationships should become supported compatibility contracts?
rationale: The RFC deliberately leaves durable product and API choices unresolved, and the repository lifecycle assigns those choices to maintainer discussion and acceptance rather than contributor or automation judgment.

options.title: Ratify the narrow catalog
options.body: Create and link the discussion, accept the command-owned CLI boundary, define the initial stable contract, create the implementation issue, and update the RFC to accepted.

options.title: Continue comparing designs
options.body: Keep the RFC open in draft while evaluating `commands` versus `catalog` and later Gateway or paired-node convergence.

options.title: Decline a new core surface
options.body: Close the proposal if existing Gateway and help surfaces should remain the only supported command-discovery contracts.

recommendation.title: Ratify the narrow catalog
recommendation.body: Create and link the discussion, accept the command-owned CLI boundary, define the initial stable contract, create the implementation issue, and update the RFC to accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: The git history ties this person most directly to the repository lifecycle that governs the required decision and acceptance steps.
